question: What is the primary purpose of performing an eye irrigation procedure?

options.A: To measure the intraocular pressure of the eyeball
options.B: To dilate the pupils for a detailed eye examination
options.C: To flush away harmful substances and foreign bodies
options.D: To deliver systemic antibiotics into the bloodstream

explanation: Irrigation mechanically removes irritating substances and chemicals from the conjunctival sac before they cause cellular damage. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h1)

question: Why is immediate eye irrigation necessary after an alkaline chemical splash?

options.A: Alkaline substances penetrate deeper and cause rapid tissue destruction
options.B: Acids are neutralized slower than alkaline agents in the eye
options.C: Chemicals immediately bind to the lens and cause cataracts
options.D: Tears wash away alkaline substances too slowly on their own

explanation: Alkalis liquefy cell membranes, allowing rapid penetration into ocular structures, making immediate dilution critical. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h1)

question: Which clinical condition makes eye irrigation strictly dangerous to perform?

options.A: Excessive mucus discharge from bacterial infection
options.B: Mild redness caused by an allergic reaction
options.C: A suspected penetrating injury of the eyeball
options.D: A small dust particle trapped under the eyelid

explanation: Pressurized fluid forced into a ruptured or penetrated globe will push debris and fluid inside, worsening internal damage. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h2)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with acid splashed into both eyes. What is the correct nursing action?

options.B: Apply an eye patch and send the patient home
options.C: Wait for the ophthalmologist to arrive first
options.D: Instill thick eye ointment to coat the cornea

explanation: Chemical splashes require immediate emergency dilution to prevent severe corneal burns and permanent vision loss. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h2)

question: Which fluid is most commonly recommended for routine eye irrigation?
explanation: Normal saline is isotonic to eye tissues, preventing osmotic injury and irritation during prolonged flushing. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h3)

question: What is the specific function of a Morgan lens during eye irrigation?

options.A: It magnifies tiny corneal scratches for easier medical diagnosis
options.B: It floats on the eye and delivers continuous steady fluid irrigation
options.C: It seals the eyelids shut to prevent any fluid from leaking out
options.D: It measures the exact chemical concentration inside the tears

explanation: A Morgan lens connects to IV tubing, allowing continuous, hands-free washing across the entire corneal and conjunctival surface. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h3)

question: Why should the patient's head be tilted toward the affected side during irrigation?

options.A: To make the patient fall asleep during the procedure
options.B: To increase the speed at which fluid drains downward
options.C: To allow the doctor to look directly into the ear canal
options.D: To prevent contaminated fluid from entering the good eye

explanation: Tilting toward the affected side ensures runoff flows outward and away, protecting the healthy eye from chemical or infectious spread. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h4)

question: What is an essential nursing action before starting an eye irrigation procedure?

options.A: Giving strong oral pain relief tablets to block all pain
options.B: Explaining the procedure to ease patient anxiety and fear
options.C: Checking the patient's blood pressure and pulse rate
options.D: Applying a tight bandage over both eyes for protection

explanation: Patients with eye injuries are often frightened; clear communication builds trust and encourages cooperation during the flush. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h4)

question: Where should the stream of irrigating fluid be directed inside the eye?

options.A: Against the lower tear duct opening to clear blockage
options.B: From the outer edge moving inward toward the nose
options.C: From the inner canthus flowing toward the outer canthus
options.D: Directly onto the center of the transparent cornea

explanation: Directing fluid from the inner to outer corner prevents washing debris or chemicals down into the tear duct system. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h5)

question: Why must the nurse apply pressure to the orbital rim when opening eyelids?

options.A: To avoid placing direct pressure on the fragile eyeball
options.B: To prevent the patient from blinking too frequently
options.C: To make the upper eyelid stick to the forehead skin
options.D: To block tear production during the irrigation process

explanation: The bony orbital rim protects the eye structures, whereas pressing directly on the globe can cause trauma or rupture. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h5)

question: What is the correct way to dry the face after finishing eye irrigation?

options.A: Pat dry gently using sterile gauze moving from inside outward
options.B: Leave the face wet so the remaining water can evaporate
options.C: Rub the eyelids hard with a rough towel to dry quickly
options.D: Use an electric hand dryer pointed directly at the face

explanation: Gentle wiping away from the nose prevents reintroducing moisture or contaminants back into the inner corner of the eye. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h6)

question: What should the nurse document immediately after completing an eye irrigation procedure?

options.A: Solution type, volume used, duration, and patient's response
options.B: Detailed financial records and hospital bed assignment
options.C: The exact brand name of the plastic kidney basin used
options.D: The patient's personal family medical and surgical history

explanation: Accurate clinical documentation records the specifics of the treatment given and evaluates the patient's immediate response. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h6)

question: Which complication can happen if the irrigation nozzle touches the eye?
explanation: Accidental contact between the equipment tip and the delicate cornea causes a scratch or abrasion on the epithelial layer. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h7)

question: What is a common temporary side effect after completing continuous eye irrigation?

options.A: Complete inability to move the eyelids up and down
options.B: Severe yellow discoloration of the white sclera
options.C: Mild blurred vision and sensitivity to bright light
options.D: Total permanent loss of peripheral vision fields

explanation: Residual fluid and mild irritation commonly cause temporary blurring and photophobia that resolve shortly after the procedure. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h7)
